units.label: CSS (and SCSS)
units.pins: No product pin — CSS is versioned by browser Baseline. firefox 153.0.3 is FROZEN (measurement instrument, not a target).
units.currency: Firefox 153.0.3 → 156.0.1 is reported as information only (frozen by design; re-measuring is a decision, not drift).
units.notes: The 'LTS' equivalent is Baseline (web.dev/baseline + the web-features dataset): Widely available vs Newly available, by year. Identify which Baseline year the content applies up to, then list every CSS feature that became Baseline Newly/Widely available 2023 → 2026 (e.g. nesting, :has(), container queries & container style queries, @layer, @scope, subgrid, color-mix(), relative colors, light-dark(), @property, @starting-style, transition-behavior allow-discrete, interpolate-size / calc-size, anchor positioning, view transitions, scroll-driven animations, text-wrap balance/pretty, field-sizing, popover/:popover-open, content-visibility, if(), corner-shape, sibling-index() — take the real list and status from web.dev / MDN browser-compat, not this note). SCSS (phase 10): Dart Sass 1.x → module system, @import deprecation and removal timeline (sass-lang.com/documentation/breaking-changes) — include.

units.label: Vite (and Rolldown / Oxc)
units.pins: vite {source npm:vite, pin 8.2.2, checked 2026-09-07} · rolldown 1.2.7 · esbuild 0.28.2
units.notes: Vite's support policy (vite.dev/releases): the latest minor gets fixes, previous majors get important fixes/security for a period — use it and endoflife.date. Compare 5 → 6 (Environment API) → 7 (Node floor, baseline-widely-available default target) → 8 (Rolldown + Oxc unified bundler, removed options) → 8.x latest, from vite.dev/blog + github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/vite/CHANGELOG.md. 🔴 Topic 05 is literally named 'build-system-rollup' — check whether the pages still teach Rollup as Vite's production bundler (CONTRADICTED if so without a v8 note). Imported 2026-08-14; A2 validation lane has 70 units pending for imported tracks — this audit does not validate prose, only version coverage.

units.label: Webpack (and Rspack)
units.currency: Webpack 5.110.3 → 5.111.1 (minor) · Rspack 2.2.2 → 2.2.7 (patch). 🔴 Rspack has ZERO mentions across the corpus (noted 2026-09-07).
units.notes: Webpack has no LTS; 5.x is the only line (check github.com/webpack/webpack/releases for 5.90 → latest and any webpack 6 roadmap/announcement). Compare notable 5.x additions (CSS experiments, lazy compilation, ESM output, `import.meta` features, persistent cache changes, deprecations) and the ecosystem shifts that change what a developer writes: Rspack 1.0 → 2.x as a drop-in replacement, webpack-dev-server 5, Module Federation 2.0 (@module-federation/enhanced). Imported track; no version spines.

units.label: Babel
units.notes: Babel has no LTS; Babel 7 maintenance status after Babel 8 stable (check babeljs.io/docs/v8-migration and the Babel blog for Babel 7's support end). Compare 7.2x → 8.0 → 8.0.x: ESM-only packages, Node floor, removed plugins/options (e.g. loose mode changes, proposal plugins moved, preset-env defaults, targets/browserslist behaviour, @babel/polyfill gone, JSX runtime default automatic, TS preset changes) — take the list from the v8 migration guide and changelog. Also the React Compiler shipping as a Babel plugin, if pages teach it. Imported track (19 files); no version spines.
